en: The Eight Verses on Śiva by Mārkaṇḍeya

I worship Śiva, the Lord of Gaurī, who always dwells near the banks of the Godāvarī; the Lord of Creatures, the Generous One, the Sovereign of All, the Bestower of Boons, whose sole purpose is the accomplishment of the aims of the virtuous; who bears the moon, whose feet are worshipped by the infinite, whose forehead is smeared with the ashes of Mārkaṇḍeya, and who is the auspicious dancer. I worship the Lord of the Universe, the illustrious Viśveśa, the sinless Master of all worlds, who eternally resides on Mount Kailāsa as His own abode, who has manifested His supreme splendor, and who is accompanied by His chariot.
I worship Naṭeśa, Gaurīśa, whose eyes are as graceful as the sun, the moon, and fire...

2 I worship Mahādeva, the All, the friend of Madhuripu, the bringer of auspiciousness, the Supreme Śambhu, accompanied by Ambā, the Destroyer of Cities, the Lord who removes worldly existence; the enemy of Smara, the Omniscient, the Destroyer of Smara, the Beginningless, the Wielder of the Deer-mark... 3
I worship Him whose heart at twilight is filled with the most powerful triple symphony (of song, dance, and instrument) by thirty-three crores of the most excellent gods,
who performs the *ullāsya* dance for Ramā, Vāṇī, Indra, Śrīpati, and Brahmā...
[And] I worship the Preceptor of the Gods, whose neck is like a blue lotus upon the crimson splendor of Bhavānī’s heart-lotus, and who dwells eternally within the thousand-petaled lotus of her heart.
I worship the one who bestows all happiness upon the praises of devotees, the perfectly stable state...

5 You are Śiva; you are Viṣṇu; you are the entirety of the universe; you are the sun and the moon; you are the sky; you are the body; you are the Self of the entire world, O Lord! You are the ascetic; you are the goal at the end; you are the most blissful totality [as taught] by the eminent Jaiminis. I worship you. 6
I worship with loud invocation "Hara, Hara, Hara! through my speech; always with devotion and joy, "Śiva, Śiva, Śiva! within my mind;
and repeatedly with fear, the praise "Bhavabhava, Abhava!"...
I worship You, who are invoked when afraid, praised by the best of sages, the remover of bonds, the one who exists as the true devotee, and who protects the child out of compassion.

I worship Mārkaṇḍeya, the Lord Paraśiva, who is the refuge of devotees and the supreme goal. (8) Yajñeśa Bhūsura, the moon from the ocean of the noble lineage of Śrī Kolācala, has composed this *Mārkaṇḍeyaśivāṣṭaka*. (9)
